papers.abstract: The PERSONA-Ovary study evaluated germline pathogenic/likely-pathogenic variant prevalence, feasibility of unselected multigene testing integration in routine clinical care, and germline-somatic BRCA concordance in ovarian cancer patients. We conducted a prospective observational study of consecutive ovarian carcinoma patients treated at a tertiary-cancer care center, between July 2018 and September 2021. Germline multigene panel testing was performed using next-generation sequencing. Feasibility was assessed by informative rate and turnaround time. Germline-somatic concordance was assessed in patients with paired tumor BRCA results. Among 320 patients, pathogenic/likely-pathogenic variants were identified in 95 (29.7%, 95% CI 24.7-35.0); 81 (85.3%, 95% CI 76.5-91.7) carried mutations in ovarian cancer susceptibility genes, including 60 with BRCA alterations (63.2%, BRCA1 n=43, BRCA2 n=17). Germline testing was informative in all patients (100%). Median turnaround time was 221days (IQR 173-284), improving significantly across study periods (p<0.001). Tumor BRCA testing was available in 298 patients (93.1%), with germline-somatic concordance of 94.0% (κ=0.82, 95% CI 0.72-0.90). A germline-first strategy with reflex tumor testing achieved complete detection with fewer assays than parallel testing; a tumor-first strategy required the fewest assays (366 vs 596) but missed two germline BRCA carriers (detection rate of 96.3%). Unselected germline multigene panel testing was technically feasible and clinically informative in routine ovarian cancer care. Pathogenic/likely-pathogenic variants were identified in 29.7% of patients, supporting germline testing integration into contemporary ovarian cancer management. Although germline-first strategies maximize hereditary cancer detection, dedicated molecular workflows remain necessary to ensure clinically actionable turnaround times.

papers.abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is a leading cause of cancer-related mortality worldwide. However, comprehensive population-level data describing etiologic patterns, treatment exposure, healthcare utilisation, and survival remain limited in many countries. This study aimed to characterise the national burden, care patterns, and outcomes of HCC in Turkey. We performed a nationwide, real-world analysis of adult patients diagnosed with HCC between 2016 and 2024 using administrative health data. Cases were identified by an administrative case definition requiring at least three separate records of ICD-10 codes C22, C22.0, or C22.9; at least one C22.0 code was not required, so HCC could not be confirmed at the individual level. Baseline comorbidities were restricted to conditions recorded on or before the date of diagnosis. Demographic characteristics, underlying liver disease, etiologic factors, treatment exposure, and the level and type of diagnosing institution were assessed. Overall survival (OS) was estimated using the Kaplan-Meier method. To reduce immortal-time bias, treatment exposure was analysed in a three-month landmark cohort; because treatment dates were unavailable, this reduces but does not eliminate the bias. Multivariable Cox regression was performed within the same cohort. A total of 13,674 patients (64.6% male; median age 64 years, IQR 55-73) were included, of whom 61.4% had died at the data cutoff; median follow-up was 53.0 months. The median OS was 13.2 months (95% CI 12.1-14.5), with 1-, 3-, and 5-year OS of 50.9%, 41.1%, and 36.9%; because patients dying before three qualifying records accumulated could not enter the cohort, these estimates apply to patients meeting the case-identification algorithm and are likely to overstate population survival. OS was markedly longer in women than in men (median 50.9 vs 8.2 months), and longer in patients without cirrhosis recorded at diagnosis than in those with cirrhosis (18.5 vs 9.0 months; both P < 0.001). Hepatitis B was the most frequently recorded specific etiology (29.4%); among mutually exclusive categories, NAFLD-associated HCC had the most favourable survival (5-year OS 61.0%) and alcohol-related HCC the least (median 8.8 months), while HBV-HDV co-infection was associated with longer survival than HBV mono-infection (58.2 vs 12.0 months; P < 0.001), a difference that persisted after adjustment for age, sex, and cirrhosis; no specific etiology could be assigned in 56.1% of patients. Sensitivity analyses restricting etiologic ascertainment to codes recorded within 3 months before to 3 months after diagnosis, or incorporating viral serology, attenuated the survival of the specific viral etiologies, indicating survival-dependent ascertainment. In a multivariable Cox model fitted in the three-month landmark cohort (n = 8958), older age, male sex, cirrhosis, and systemic therapy were associated with higher mortality (all P < 0.001), with time-varying associations for age, cirrhosis, and systemic therapy. The association of local therapy with mortality was not constant over follow-up (HR 0.78, 95% CI 0.72-0.85 during 0-24 months after the landmark and 1.22, 1.04-1.43 thereafter); the overall association was no longer evident after liver transplantation was excluded from the local-therapy category. Care was highly centralised within secondary and tertiary institutions. In this nationwide analysis, HCC in Turkey was characterised by limited OS and pronounced sex-based disparities, with survival differing by cirrhosis status and recorded etiology; etiologic ascertainment was itself survival-dependent, so these contrasts describe recorded categories. Hepatitis B was the most frequently recorded specific etiology, underscoring the continued importance of HBV prevention, screening, and surveillance, while HCV, HDV, alcohol-related and metabolic liver disease accounted for smaller recorded proportions; temporal trends in etiology were not analysed. Because tumour stage and liver function were unavailable, the treatment-survival associations are descriptive and subject to confounding by indication. Efforts focused on HBV control, earlier detection, risk-based surveillance of patients with cirrhosis, and improved referral pathways may improve population-level outcomes.

papers.abstract: Sensitive biomarkers for recurrence risk stratification, recurrence surveillance and adjuvant therapy guidance are of unmet need for patients with hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) undergoing liver transplantation (LT). Herein, we explored the potential of profiling circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) for prediction and prevention of recurrence in HCC after LT. HCC patients (n=91) who underwent LT were prospectively enrolled. ctDNA was assayed using next-generation sequencing from perioperative plasma (n=408). Associations between ctDNA status with clinicopathological parameters, tumor recurrence, and adjuvant treatment effect were analyzed. Higher preoperative ctDNA burden correlated with microvascular invasion (median: 45.0 vs 5.1 MTM/mL, P=0.003) and recurrence (156.2 vs 7.7 MTM/mL, P<0.001). ctDNA clearance was noted in 87.7% patients after LT and patients who kept positive postoperative ctDNA showed higher recurrence risk (HR=8.86, P<0.001), especially early recurrence (within 1 year; 75.0% vs 10.1%, P<0.001). During follow-up, positive longitudinal ctDNA was similarly predictive of recurrence (HR=36.50, P<0.001). The AUC of longitudinal ctDNA for predicting recurrence was 0.930-significantly higher than alpha-fetoprotein (0.655, P<0.001). Longitudinal ctDNA detected radiologically evidenced recurrence with a median lead time of 5.1 months compared to standard-of-care surveillance. Among patients who received adjuvant therapy, those with positive postoperative ctDNA could benefit (HR=0.11, P=0.003) and those with decreased ctDNA burden following treatment experienced longer interval from ctDNA positivity to recurrence (HR=0.17, P=0.006). Serial ctDNA analysis demonstrates strong prognostic value, capable of heralding tumor recurrence prior to radiological recurrence and measuring treatment efficacy. Its integration into clinical practice of HCC provides unique opportunities for adjuvant therapy decision-making following LT.

papers.abstract: Cancer is not biologically confined to the tumor bed. Cachexia, fatigue, metabolic dysfunction, circadian disruption, and immune dysfunction reflect disturbances that local models alone cannot fully explain. The brain is well positioned to participate in these processes because it continuously samples circulating signals and coordinates endocrine and autonomic responses. Yet the afferent side of this communication has received less attention than its downstream consequences. Here, we synthesize evidence showing that cytokines, hormones, metabolites, and cargo carried by extracellular vesicles can engage central sensory interfaces and integrative regions, particularly circumventricular organs and hypothalamic and brainstem circuits. We use the term Endocriception to describe afferent humoral sensing and early central decoding of circulating biochemical signals, and focus here on how tumor- and host-associated changes engage this process in cancer. Central neuroendocrine governance refers to the subsequent integration of this information and the generation of autonomic and endocrine outputs. Persistent inflammation, stress, circadian disruption, and impaired feedback may gradually reconfigure this regulatory system. The resulting changes can affect systemic immunity, metabolism, behavior, and host tolerance of cancer. Evidence is strongest for a limited number of pathways, whereas many proposed links remain incomplete or dependent on tumor type and experimental context. We therefore present central neuroendocrine governance as a working framework for organizing current evidence and guiding mechanistic studies, biomarker development, and interventions aimed at restoring host physiology.

papers.abstract: rVSVΔG-ZEBOV-GP vaccine is recommended for prevention of Ebola virus (EBOV) infection and disease (EVD). However, breakthrough EBOV infections have been observed in vaccinees. Currently available diagnostic and research assays cannot reliably distinguish individuals vaccinated against Ebola virus from those previously infected with the virus. This limitation complicates interpretation of vaccine-effectiveness studies, seroepidemiologic investigations, and estimates of infection or attack rates. The ability to differentiate vaccine-induced immune responses from those resulting from natural infection remains an important unmet public health and research need. We developed a multiplex sero-diagnostic assay simultaneously detecting IgA, IgG, and IgM antibodies against vesicular stomatitis Indiana virus nucleoprotein (VSV-N), a vaccine-specific marker absent in natural infection, and EBOV-GP, the vaccine's target antigen. We evaluated longitudinal samples from 30 individuals after vaccination and 30 placebo (saline) recipients, as well as 8 participants from a long-term vaccination follow-up study. We detected increase in all antibodies against both protein antigens in vaccinated individuals. Critically, the assay reveals that anti-VSV-N IgA responses emerge earlier and more robustly than anti-GP responses in vaccinees, establishing anti-N IgA as a definitive, early, and durable biomarker of rVSVΔG-ZEBOV-GP vaccination with high sensitivity and specificity. The assay enables rapid, accurate identification of vaccine recipients and supports real-time assessment of vaccine effectiveness during outbreaks. Furthermore, the assay's adaptability to the expanding pipeline of VSV-vectored vaccines positions it as a transformative diagnostic platform for accelerating preparedness for future infectious disease threats and outbreak response strategies. papers.abstract: Chimeric antigen receptor (CAR)-T cell therapy has achieved remarkable success in hematologic malignancies, but durable efficacy remains limited by insufficient CAR-T cell persistence. Here, we show that activated CAR-T cells upregulate multiple NKG2D ligands (NKG2DLs), increasing their susceptibility to natural killer (NK) cell-mediated CAR-T cell cytotoxicity. To address this vulnerability, we engineer CAR-T cells to overexpress full-length NKG2D (CAR-NG). NKG2D overexpression reduces the surface accessibility of endogenous NKG2DLs without decreasing their total protein abundance. In parallel, engagement of tumor-expressed NKG2DLs in trans provides additional costimulatory signals, enhancing CAR-T cell activation and proliferation while attenuating exhaustion-associated phenotypes. In hematologic and solid tumor models, CAR-NG cells exhibit reduced susceptibility to NK-cell-mediated cytotoxicity, improved tumor control, increased in vivo expansion, deeper tumor infiltration, and no evident additional toxicity compared with conventional CAR-T cells. These findings identify NKG2D overexpression as an engineering strategy that enhances CAR-T antitumor activity primarily through tumor NKG2DL-dependent trans costimulation.

papers.abstract: There is a paucity of high-level evidence for adjuvant radiation therapy (ART) in cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma (CSCC) creating practice variations. This study provides expert consensus recommendations on patient and tumor selection, timing, duration, dosage, and additional considerations for ART in node-negative CSCC. The Delphi panel included 35 experts in radiation oncology (15), dermatology/Mohs micrographic surgery (9), medical oncology (7), head and neck surgery (3), and surgical oncology (1). Consensus was defined as ≥80% concordance; near-consensus 70-79% concordance. Consensus was reached to recommend ART when further surgery is not possible, but the tumor has positive gross or histologic/microscopic margins (35/35, 100%). Key consensus or near-consensus recommendations for recommending ART to the tumor bed following negative-margin surgery include: 5-year cumulative incidence of local recurrence (29/35, 83%) or nodal metastasis (27/35, 77%) ≥ 20%; gross cortical bone/marrow invasion (32/35, 91%); skull base invasion (32/35, 91%); 4 risk factors (RF) (35/35, 100%); 3 RF (30-33/35, 86-94%); PNI ≥ 0.1 mm and one other RF (30/35, 86%); and clinical nerve invasion (31/35, 89%). Immune status influenced ART decision-making (30/35, 86%) with 77% (27/35) more likely to recommend ART for immunosuppressed patients. Consensus was reached to omit ART for pathologic complete response following neoadjuvant immunotherapy (34/35, 97%). Among radiation oncologists, 100% (15/15) agreed the optimal window for ART to the tumor bed is 4-8 weeks and that hypofractionated regimens can be appropriate (12/15, 80%). Consensus was reached for prescription doses of 60-66 Gy in 2 Gy/fx (15/15, 100%) or 50-55 Gy in 2.5 Gy/fx (13/15, 87%), and that superficial radiation and brachytherapy are inappropriate ART modalities for node-negative high-stage CSCC (14/15, 93%). There was no consensus on elective nodal basin irradiation. This Delphi study provides an expert consensus-based framework to standardize ART for node-negative high-stage CSCC following surgery, informing future guidelines and utilization.

papers.abstract: Ultra-hypofractionated whole-breast radiotherapy has become an accepted option for early breast cancer, but evidence on the incorporation of a simultaneous integrated boost within a five-fraction schedule remains limited. The present study evaluated five-year late side effects after whole-breast irradiation with a simultaneous integrated boost delivered in five fractions in a prospective multicentre cohort. This prospective, non-randomized, multicentre cohort included 242 patients with early breast cancer treated between April and December 2020. All patients underwent breast-conserving surgery with clear margins. Whole-breast irradiation was delivered at 26 Gy in five daily fractions, and 157 patients received a simultaneous integrated boost to 29 Gy in five fractions. The primary endpoint was late normal-tissue side effects in the simultaneous integrated boost subgroup, assessed prospectively with clinical examination, photographic documentation, and LENT-SOMA scoring. Comparisons with patients treated without a boost were exploratory. Median follow-up was 64.7 months in both the overall cohort and the simultaneous integrated boost subgroup, and 221 of 242 patients completed the scheduled five-year visit. In the simultaneous integrated boost subgroup, cumulative any-grade pain was reported in 14.6% of patients at five years, and cumulative any-grade fibrosis in 8.9%. Other late side effects were uncommon, including breast oedema in 5.1%, arm oedema in 0.6%, atrophy in 1.9%, and telangiectasia in 0.6%; no ulceration was observed. In exploratory unadjusted analyses, pain was more frequent in the simultaneous integrated boost group than in the no-boost group, whereas no significant differences were observed for other late side effects. Chemotherapy receipt was also associated with persistent pain in exploratory analyses. Whole-breast irradiation with a 29 Gy simultaneous integrated boost in five fractions achieved low rates of objective late side effects and reassuring oncological outcomes after more than five years, while shortening treatment to a single one-week course compared with sequential or moderately hypofractionated schedules. Persistent low-grade breast pain was more frequent with the boost, but non-randomized allocation and its association with chemotherapy preclude causal attribution, supporting continued, careful use in selected patients alongside further prospective, randomized studies with baseline symptom assessment.

papers.abstract: Colorectal cancer (CRC) is characterized by marked epithelial heterogeneity and dynamic tumor-microenvironment interactions. However, epithelial states associated with progression across the normal-adenoma-carcinoma sequence remain incompletely defined. Single-cell RNA sequencing data from normal colorectal mucosa, adenoma, and tumor tissues were analyzed using inferCNV, Monocle, Slingshot, CytoTRACE, CellChat, and SCENIC. An OLFM4⁺ tumor cell risk score (OTRS) was constructed using Cox and LASSO regression, and TIMP1 function was evaluated in vitro. Eight major cell types and nine tumor epithelial subtypes were identified. C3 OLFM4⁺ cells showed elevated transcriptional activity, stemness, metabolic activity, and greater representation in carcinoma than adenoma tissues. Trajectory analyses positioned these cells in an early-to-intermediate transitional state. CellChat predicted prominent fibroblast-C3 OLFM4⁺ interactions, including a putative WNT2B-FZD/LRP axis, while SCENIC identified XBP1, NFIA, PPARG, HDAC2, and UBE2K as subtype-associated regulators. The C3 OLFM4⁺-derived OTRS stratified prognosis; high OTRS was associated with poorer survival, macrophage-enriched infiltration, higher stromal, immune, and TIDE scores, and differential predicted drug sensitivity. TIMP1 knockdown suppressed malignant behaviors in CRC cells. C3 OLFM4⁺ cells represent a stem-like, metabolically active tumor epithelial state associated with CRC progression, fibroblast-derived WNT signaling, immune-evasion-related features, and unfavorable prognosis. The OTRS model may support prognostic and therapeutic assessment, while TIMP1 contributes to malignant CRC cell behavior.

papers.abstract: To examine temporal trends in immunotherapy (IO) adoption and identify factor-related disparities among older adults with advanced endometrial cancer (EC). We conducted a retrospective cohort study using the National Cancer Database (NCDB), including women aged ≥65 years diagnosed with stage III-IV EC between 2019 and 2023. Temporal trends of IO use were assessed, and multivariable logistic regression identified predictors of IO utilization. Among 38,931 patients with advanced EC, 21,272 (54.6%) were aged ≥65 years. IO utilization increased significantly over time across all age groups (P-trend <0.001). By 2023, 1851 older adults (40%) received IO, but utilization remained substantially lower among patients aged ≥85 years (55/255, 21.6%; P < 0.001). On multivariable analysis, patients aged ≥85 years were significantly less likely to receive IO compared with those aged 65-74 years (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 0.41; 95% CI, 0.32-0.52; P < 0.001). Non-Hispanic (NH)-Black (aOR 0.81; 95% CI, 0.73-0.90; P < 0.001) and Hispanic patients (aOR 0.84; 95% CI, 0.71-0.99; P = 0.034) were also less likely to receive IO compared with NH-White patients. After adjustment for socioeconomic factors, NH-Black was 12% less likely to receive IO (aOR 0.88; 95% CI, 0.77-0.99; P = 0.0034). Despite the proven clinical benefit of IO use for patients with advanced EC, substantial age-based disparities persist. A lower likelihood of IO receipt among NH-Black compared with NH-White patients was also observed even after adjustment for socioeconomic factors. These findings highlight the need for further investigation into clinical, socioeconomic, and structural barriers influencing treatment access in older and minoritized populations.

papers.abstract: The specific mechanisms of Verbascoside (VB) in ovarian cancer (OC) remain insufficient. This study aimed to explore the anti-tumor mechanisms of VB in OC, focusing on its ability to modulate the immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment (TME), particularly through targeting neutrophil infiltration and neutrophil extracellular traps (NETs). The anti-tumor and anti-NETosis efficacy of VB was evaluated in vivo using subcutaneous, orthotopic, and pulmonary metastasis mouse models of OC. Microproteomics and bioinformatics analysis identified the direct molecular target of VB and the key neutrophil chemoattractant. The underlying mechanisms were validated in vitro and in vivo (using SKOV3, ID8, and neutrophils), alongside loss-of-function approaches. The combination of VB with anti-PD-1 immunotherapy was also assessed. VB inhibited OC proliferation/metastasis, promoted anti-tumor immunity, and suppressed neutrophil infiltration and NETosis. Neutrophil depletion attenuated VB's anti-metastatic effect. Microproteomics and bioinformatics screening identified IRAK4 as a direct molecular target of VB and CXCL5 as a key neutrophil chemoattractant. SPR confirmed the direct binding between VB and IRAK4, and molecular docking revealed specific hydrogen bond interactions. Mechanistically, VB treatment or IRAK4 knockdown suppressed CXCL5 expression, and consequently reduced neutrophil infiltration and NETosis. Consistently, CXCL5 overexpression abrogated the inhibitory effects of VB on neutrophil NETosis and recruitment. Furthermore, VB synergized with anti-PD-1 therapy, thereby achieving superior tumor growth inhibition, reduced Ki67 expression, and enhanced CD8+ T cell infiltration. In conclusion, VB exerts potent anti-tumor effects in OC by targeting the IRAK4/CXCL5 axis, thereby inhibiting neutrophil infiltration and NETosis, reshaping the immunosuppressive TME, and restoring anti-tumor immunity.

papers.abstract: Macrophages are among the most versatile differentiated cell types in the body, serving as key regulators of tissue development, homeostasis, inflammation, repair, and immunity. Their functional diversity cannot be captured by fixed subsets, binary activation states, or single-marker definitions. Macrophage identity emerges instead from the integration of developmental origin, tissue niche, epigenetic history, local environmental cues, and disease-associated signals. Advances in single-cell genomics, spatial profiling, epigenomics, in vivo perturbation, and computational modeling now show that this behavior is organized through modular gene programs, so that any given macrophage state is best described as a weighted combination of program activities rather than a discrete label. We argue that embracing this modular architecture matters not only for annotation but for therapy: macrophage-directed interventions will require defining disease-associated states, identifying surface-accessible entry points into them, and rewiring the underlying programs with spatial and temporal precision.

papers.abstract: The role of senescent tumor cells in modulating the immune microenvironment and influencing immunotherapy efficacy remains poorly understood. In this study, we investigate the function of the senescence-associated gene membrane magnesium transporter 1 (MMGT1) in triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) immunotherapy. MMGT1 is upregulated in TNBC and correlates with poor prognosis. Mammary gland-specific knockout of Mmgt1 significantly impedes tumor growth. Mechanistically, MMGT1 promotes lipid metabolism by facilitating translocation of the SCAP-SREBP1 complex to the Golgi apparatus, thereby suppressing cellular senescence. Notably, senescent TNBC cells enhance CD8+ T cell proliferation and cytotoxicity through CCL20 secretion. Furthermore, a positive feedback loop exists between MMGT1 and SREBP1. In vivo, AZ191 downregulates MMGT1 expression, which suppresses tumor growth and enhances the efficacy of anti-PD-1 therapy. Collectively, these findings reveal a critical role for MMGT1 in shaping the TNBC immune microenvironment and suggest that targeting MMGT1 represents a promising strategy to improve anti-PD-1 immunotherapy outcomes.

papers.abstract: Lung-protective ventilation in acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) remains under-applied at the bedside, partly due to the absence of integrated, context-aware decision-support tools. Large language models (LLMs) with advanced code generation capabilities have created a new possibility: physicians can now build the bedside tools they need without depending on software vendors or programming expertise. This practice, broadly termed "vibe coding", has entered medical discourse but has not been formally evaluated as a clinical competency. We report the development of VentiProtect ARDS, a real-time ventilator titration assistant built by a single physician in a single session of 4 minutes 25 seconds, as a proof-of-concept for physician prompt engineering: the structured translation of clinical knowledge into a natural-language specification that constrains LLM code generation. A structured eight-block prompt was developed through an iterative pre-prompt reasoning process and submitted to Claude Opus 4.6 via the Antigravity agentic development environment. The generated application computes predicted body weight, tidal volume, driving pressure, respiratory system compliance, mechanical power, and oxygenation index, with real-time colour-coded alerts and an active suggestion engine that calculates exact corrective ventilator settings. Formula accuracy was verified using an independent automated test suite of 100 scenarios (1,400 individual checks) with no computational errors identified. The tool runs locally with no installation, network dependency, or patient data transmission. This proof-of-concept suggests that physician prompt engineering may represent a potential clinical competency that does not require programming experience, although a single self-performed case cannot establish it across physicians. The LLM generates syntax. The physician generates medicine.

papers.abstract: Acute respiratory acid-base changes induce pH-dependent electrolyte redistribution. Although this response has been characterised in vitro, the in vivo changes depend on multicompartment buffering and remain poorly defined. We conducted a multicentre retrospective study of patients undergoing apnoea testing for organ donation after determination of brain death, a clinical model allowing in vivo study of acute ventilatory changes. The primary outcome was the pH-dependent change in strong ion difference (SID). Secondary analyses examined individual electrolytes, pH-SID effect modification by physiological variables, and how well the derived model agreed with observed SID changes compared with a simple bedside pH-correction method (ΔSID=-15×ΔpH). In 263 participants, pH decreased from 7.40 (0.07) to 7.23 (0.07) and returned to 7.40 (0.08). Per pH unit increase, SID changed by -11.7 meq L-1 (95% CI -13.1 to -10.3; P<0.001), driven primarily by sodium ion (Na) (52% of change -7.2 mM; P<0.001) and chloride ion (Cl) (36% of change +3.7 mM; P<0.001). Higher haemoglobin concentration was associated with a higher pH-dependent SID change, together explaining 53% of within-patient variability. Agreement between predicted and observed SID changes was only modestly improved by using the derived model vs a simplified pH-correction model (sd of differences 1.74 vs 1.92 meq L-1). Acute respiratory acid-base disturbances produce in vivo Na and Cl redistribution associated with pH change that are modulated by haemoglobin concentration. The observed pH-dependent electrolyte redistribution is consistent with physiological buffering and can be reasonably approximated using a simple bedside pH-correction model.

papers.abstract: P-loop and αC-helix compressing (PACC) mutations comprise a structurally distinct subgroup of epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) mutations in non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) with limited treatment options. Firmonertinib is a once-daily oral, brain-penetrant, mutant-selective EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitor with a unique trifluoroethoxy side chain. Firmonertinib had high anti-proliferative efficacy in EGFR PACC-mutant cells and xenografts. In the phase 1b FURTHER study (NCT05364073), patients with metastatic EGFR PACC-mutant NSCLC randomized to receive first-line firmonertinib 160 mg (n = 25) or 240 mg (n = 22) had confirmed objective response rates (ORRs) of 43% and 68%, median duration of response not reached and 14.6 months, and median progression-free survival of 11.1 and 16.0 months, respectively; treatment-related adverse events led to dose reductions (19% and 24%) and discontinuation (3% and 0%). Intracranial ORR among patients with brain metastases at baseline was 47% (8/17). Results support further study of first-line firmonertinib in patients with EGFR PACC-mutant NSCLC.

papers.abstract: Patients from more deprived backgrounds experience poorer postoperative outcomes. We analysed preoperative characteristics in UK Perioperative Quality Improvement Programme participants according to socioeconomic position to explore opportunities for targeted interventions. Participants were adults aged ≥18 yr undergoing major elective surgery at UK Perioperative Quality Improvement Programme sites. Socioeconomic position was determined using postcode data and the Index of Multiple Deprivation (IMD) standardised aggregate scale of area-level deprivation. Associations between IMD position and patient characteristics, health behaviours, and comorbidities were analysed using descriptive statistics with appropriate parametric and nonparametric testing. Of 55 938 participants included, quintile 1 (most deprived) represented the smallest subgroup (14.2%), with recruitment varying by region and site. Median age was 66 yr with IMD 1 participants 5 yr younger (62 yr) than IMD 5 (67 yr). Deprivation gradients (IMD 5 to 1) were seen for home ownership, occupation, and educational attainment. Prevalences of smoking, inactivity, and obesity increased from IMD 5 to 1. Higher prevalences of major long-term conditions including diabetes mellitus, heart failure, stroke, and ASA physical status 3-4 were observed in more deprived quintiles. Prevalence rates of dementia and renal impairment were similar across quintiles despite the age gradient. Notably, the proportions of patients living with frailty and disability increased with deprivation. Patients presenting for major surgery from more deprived backgrounds do so in poorer overall health. They can encounter barriers to both research participation and available preoperative support. Addressing this unmet need to prevent widening perioperative health inequalities requires interventions tailored to the patient's socioeconomic context.

papers.abstract: Some women receiving epidural labour analgesia become hyperthermic. Assuming a causal mechanism, denser and more extensive sympathetic blocks might promote hyperthermia by inhibiting sweating. We therefore tested the hypothesis that hyperthermia is most common when epidural blocks are particularly effective, as indicated by excellent analgesia. In this multicentre prospective observational study, we enrolled nulliparous women with term cephalic singleton pregnancies who planned vaginal delivery with epidural analgesia. Pain intensity was assessed using an 11-point numerical rating scale (0-10) during uterine contractions before analgesia, at 10, 30, and 60 min after initiating analgesia, and then hourly until the end of the third stage, and calculated as time-weighted average, average, area under the curve, and peak scores. Our primary endpoint was intrapartum hyperthermia (≥38°C). Intrapartum hyperthermia occurred in 13% (124/952) of participants (median age 29 yr). After adjustment for confounding factors, lower pain intensity was associated with higher odds of intrapartum hyperthermia across all four measures: time-weighted average (odds ratio 1.64; 95% CI 1.40-1.91; P<0.001), average (1.56; 1.35-1.81; P<0.001), area under the curve (1.05; 1.03-1.07; P<0.001), and peak scores (1.19; 1.09-1.30; P<0.001). The identified inflection points were a time-weighted average score ≤3 points (odds ratio 8.67; 95% CI 4.19-17.9; P<0.001), average score ≤3 points (6.63; 3.56-12.3; P<0.001), area under the curve ≤30 point⋅h (13.0; 3.75-45.0; P<0.001), and peak score ≤4 points (2.53; 1.65-3.89; P<0.001), all of which were associated with increased intrapartum hyperthermia. Among nulliparous women receiving epidural analgesia for labour, lower pain scores were associated with higher odds of hyperthermia. Extensive sympathetic blockade may promote maternal hyperthermia. papers.abstract: Postoperative delirium (POD) is a frequent and serious complication, particularly in older adults undergoing major surgery. Pharmacologic prevention remains limited. This study aimed to evaluate whether perioperative ketamine or esketamine reduces POD incidence and to explore optimal administration strategies. We systematically searched PubMed, Embase, and Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials (CENTRAL) from inception to January 2025 for randomized controlled trials (RCTs) comparing perioperative ketamine or esketamine with placebo or standard care. The primary outcome was POD incidence (risk ratio [RR]). Subgroup, meta‑regression, and trial sequential analysis (TSA) were performed. Sensitivity analyses addressed active comparators and unit‑of‑analysis issues. Twenty-five RCTs (3344 patients) were included (ketamine: 9; esketamine: 16). Both agents reduced POD risk versus control (ketamine: RR 0.69, 95% CI, 0.49-0.98, P = .04; esketamine: RR 0.58, 95% CI, 0.36-0.95, P = .03). Benefit was more evident with high-dose regimens (single bolus: ketamine >0.5 mg/kg or esketamine >0.25 mg/kg; cumulative dose: ketamine >1.0 mg/kg or esketamine >0.5 mg/kg), bolus-plus-infusion, and in major surgery. The effect was observed when POD was assessed 2 to 7 days postoperatively, but not within 24 hours. TSA indicated that current evidence remains inconclusive due to insufficient information size. Dizziness risk increased (RR 1.45, 95% CI, 1.14-1.84, P = .002), while postoperative depressive symptoms decreased (RR 0.78, 95% CI, 0.63-0.96, P = .02; based on 2 studies, 493 patients). Perioperative ketamine and esketamine show a potential signal for POD reduction, particularly with optimized dosing in high‑risk patients. However, the evidence is currently inconclusive, and increased dizziness risk precludes routine recommendation. Large, multicenter RCTs are urgently needed.

papers.abstract: Elderly patients with spinal metastases are often considered poor candidates for aggressive local therapy, due in part to medical comorbidity and limited evidence to guide treatment selection. This study evaluated outcomes following spine stereotactic body radiation therapy (SBRT) in this patient population and examined predictors of local failure (LF) and vertebral compression fracture (VCF). A prospectively maintained database of consecutive patients aged ≥ 70 years with available imaging who underwent spine SBRT at a quaternary referral center from 2002 to 2024 was analyzed. The median single-fraction dose was 16 Gy (range: 12-18 Gy), and multi-fraction regimens ranged from 18 to 35 Gy in 2-5 fractions. Of 208 metastases in 161 patients (median age: 75 years, range: 70-94 years), 72% had prior conventional radiotherapy and 76% received a single fraction. The 6-, 12-, 24-, and 36-month cumulative incidence rates were 6%, 9%, 9%, and 10% for LF and 4%, 7%, 8%, and 9% for VCF (median follow-up: 9 months, range: 1-132 months). Gross tumor volume > 37 cc (subdistribution hazard ratio [sHR]: 6.27, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 1.48-26.63, P = 0.013) and Spinal Instability Neoplastic Score (SINS, per-point sHR: 1.23, 95% CI: 1.07-1.42, P = 0.005) were independently associated with LF; only SINS was independently associated with VCF (per-point sHR: 1.19, 95% CI: 1.06-1.34, P = 0.003), and 11 of 17 VCFs required cement augmentation or surgery. Age was associated with overall survival (hazard ratio: 1.05 per year, 95% CI: 1.01-1.09, P = 0.018); no statistically significant association was detected with LF or VCF when age was analyzed continuously, at thresholds of 75 or 80 years, or by exploratory maximally selected rank statistical analysis. Complete or partial pain response followed 61 of 148 evaluable treatments (41%) among 186 symptomatic metastases, and 18% of patients had grade 1-2 radiation toxicity. Spine SBRT, predominantly single-fraction reirradiation, was associated with low rates of LF and VCF; chronologic age alone should not preclude its use in appropriately selected elderly patients.

papers.abstract: Contrast enhancement is generally considered an adverse prognostic feature in adult glioma. However, its significance in newly diagnosed grade 2 IDH-mutant glioma remains uncertain, with important implications for use of the mutant IDH inhibitor vorasidenib. We evaluated survival outcomes associated with preoperative enhancement in this population. We retrospectively evaluated consecutive patients with grade 2 IDH-mutant glioma treated at two institutions between 2010 and 2021. Preoperative MRIs were assessed for intratumoral enhancement by two independent readers with third-reader adjudication. Overall survival (OS) and progression-free survival (PFS) were evaluated by Kaplan-Meier analysis, univariate and multivariable Cox regression. Among 325 evaluable patients, median age was 37 years, 47% had 1p/19q-codeletion, and 35% had gross-total resection. Median follow-up was 10.5 years. Preoperative enhancement was observed in 53 (16%) patients, most commonly nonmeasurable (72%) or ill-defined (62%); most (87%) had no residual postoperative enhancement. Preoperative enhancement was not associated with OS or PFS in either univariate analyses (OS HR 1.16 [0.67-2.01], p = 0.591; PFS HR 1.25 [0.88-1.80], p = 0.216) or multivariable analyses adjusting for established prognostic factors (OS HR 0.86 [0.46-1.61], p = 0.633; PFS HR 1.29 [0.86-1.92], p = 0.219). Enhancement characteristics (measurable size, well-defined morphology) were not associated with OS. In grade 2 IDH-mutant glioma, preoperative enhancement was not associated with OS or PFS. These findings suggest that preoperative enhancement does not identify a higher-risk subgroup in this population, and that its presence alone should not preclude consideration of vorasidenib in eligible patients.

papers.abstract: Diffuse gliomas are frequently associated with epilepsy, particularly in low-grade variants. Seizures are key events to be considered in glioma management, including during surgery. Optimizing resection of epileptic areas may affect not only postoperative epilepsy but also glioma prognosis in the context of interactions between glioma growth and neuronal activities. As for glioma tissue resection, surgery of epileptic networks requires a deeper understanding of their organization and reliable biomarkers. We investigated the spatiotemporal dynamics of the transition from interictal to ictal-like events (ILEs) using ex vivo human peritumoral tissue from glioma patients. Slices were recorded with multi-electrode arrays during the transition from the spontaneous interictal state to pharmacologically induced seizures considering the dynamics of slow versus fast oscillatory neuronal activities. Transition to seizure was characterized by the emergence of preictal discharges (PIDs), allowing subdivision of the preictal phase into build-up, steady-state, and trigger periods. PIDs progressively increased in amplitude, duration, and slope with significant changes during the trigger phase. Concurrently, high-frequency activity (180-550 Hz) and high-frequency oscillations (HFOs) increased across the transition period, particularly during the trigger phase. In addition to such preictal recruitment, the reinforcement of HFOs was accompanied by a spatial organization in additive microdomains, peaking at seizure onset and encompassing slow field potential dynamics. In the periglioma human cortex, seizures arise from progressively recruited neuronal assemblies sculpted together with HFOs, providing new insights into the microphysiological processes of glioma-related ictogenesis and requiring consideration of the preictal fast and focal neuronal activity.

papers.abstract: RAS mutations are recurrent in acute myeloid leukemia (AML); yet, their genomic and clinical landscape remain poorly characterized. We analyzed centralized molecular profiling data in 8,553 patients with newly diagnosed AML. Of these, 1,775 (21%) harbored RAS mutations: NRAS in 1,103 (13%), KRAS in 445 (5%), and both in 227 (3%). RAS mutations primarily clustered in P-loop hotspots (G12/G13, 70%), with NRAS showing higher Q61 mutation prevalence (24% vs. 9%) and KRAS showing additional K117/A146 hotspots. Multiple RAS mutations occurred in 23% of patients. Convergent evolution of RAS signaling mutations emerged as a key feature of RASmut AML. RTK/RAS pathway mutations were non-uniformly enriched: PTPN11, KIT and FLT3-TKD mutations were positively associated, CBL mutations showed no association, and FLT3-ITD mutations were negatively associated. The prognostic impact of RAS mutations was dependent on the genomic background and treatment. In multivariate analyses in intensively treated patients, NRAS mutations showed opposing associations with overall survival (OS): adverse in patients with AML, myelodysplasia-related (HR=1.32, p=0.036) and favorable in those with NPM1 (HR=0.61, p=0.036) or FLT3-ITD (HR=0.63, p=0.048) mutations, among others. KRAS mutations predicted inferior OS (HR=1.41; p=0.003). In patients treated with non-intensive, venetoclax-based regimens, RAS mutations were associated with markedly inferior OS in patients with NPM1 (HR=2.98, p=0.007) or IDH1/2 mutations (HR=4.06, p<0.001). These data inform risk stratification and development of RAS-targeting strategies in AML.

papers.abstract: Gene therapy for hemophilia A (HA) aims to provide durable hemostatic control and reduce treatment burden, but AAV-based products to date have limitations: inconsistent peak expression, declining factor levels, and immunogenicity causing transaminitis and expression loss. ASC618 (ASC Therapeutics, Milpitas, CA, USA) was developed as a second-generation gene therapy product to overcome some of these limitations, using ET3, a bioengineered chimeric human/porcine B-domain-deleted FVIII transgene, paired with a minimal liver promoter and liver codon optimization. In a phase 1/2 trial (NCT04676048), two patients received ASC618. Despite initial factor expression, both developed high-titer FVIII inhibitors and are now maintained on emicizumab prophylaxis. Although inhibitor titers have declined, both remain high-titer nearly two years after a single infusion. The best explanation for inhibitor formation is that the novel FVIII with the human-porcine hybrid construct (ET3) contained epitopes for which these patients had not developed tolerance despite both having more than 1000 exposure days to exogenous FVIII in the past. Although this trial has been halted, these cases provide important lessons for the development of future hemophilia gene therapies. They highlight the need for careful immunogenicity assessment when using bioengineered transgenes, even in previously treated patients with extensive factor VIII exposure.

papers.abstract: Ischemic reperfusion injury (IRI) during liver transplantation is associated with recurrence of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). Machine perfusion (MP) is associated with a decreased risk of IRI complications. Our study evaluated the role of MP in post-transplant oncologic outcomes in patients with HCC. Adults with HCC transplanted between 2015-2025 from the United Network for Organ Sharing database were divided into MP and no-MP groups. Propensity score matching (PSM) was also performed. Post-transplant HCC recurrence (competing risk) and overall survival (OS) were assessed. Subgroup analysis was performed in populations within and beyond the Milan criteria. A total of 19,466 patients were included in this study. MP was used in 1,392 (7.2%). The MP group had shorter waitlist times, older donors, and more frequent DCDs (p=0.001). After PSM, 512 patients were included in each group (336 patients within Milan criteria in each). In the population beyond Milan after PSM (n=352), MP use was associated with a reduced risk of 1-year and 3-year HCC recurrence (adjusted hazard ratio (aHR) 0.09, p=0.02; aHR 0.27, p=0.02). MP use was not associated with the 1-year or 3-year OS (aHR 1.34, p=0.64; aHR 1.32, p=0.54). MP may potentially reduce the risk of HCC recurrence in recipients beyond Milan criteria, without significant difference in OS. However, as MP utilization increases, further validation into the role of MP and oncologic outcomes in larger cohort studies are required.

papers.abstract: Contemporary gastroenteropancreatic neuroendocrine tumor (GEPNET) management guidelines recommend routine use of functional imaging preoperatively, but there are few data highlighting trends in functional imaging adoption. This report reviews 24 years of neuroendocrine tumor (NET) experience to describe changes in rates of preoperative functional imaging use and highlights performance differences between functional imaging types in small bowel NETs (SBNET) and pancreatic NETs (PNETs). A retrospective single-institution study from 2000 to 2023 identified patients with SBNETs and PNETs treated with surgical resection, cytoreduction, or both who underwent preoperative functional imaging. The primary measurements were frequency of functional imaging use and location of metastases identified on preoperative imaging. The study included 392 SBNET and 208 PNET patients. Preoperative functional imaging was performed for 248 (63.3%) SBNET patients (158 somatostatin receptor [SSTR] positron emission tomography [PET] and 90 Octreoscan) and 113 (54.3%) PNET patients (47 SSTR PET and 66 Octreoscan). There was a significant positive trend over time in functional imaging use in SBNET patients, with an approximate 2.5% yearly increase (p < 0.01) but no significant change in PNET patients during the course of the study (p = 0.82). At presentation, 82.3% (204/248) of the SBNET patients and 54.9% (62/113) of the PNET patients had metastatic disease. Compared with Octreoscan, SSTR PET more frequently identified bone and retroperitoneal nodal metastases. Rates of functional imaging use in SBNET patients but not in PNET patients increased significantly during the last 24 years. Patients with SBNETs and PNETs frequently presented with metastatic disease, and SSTR-based functional imaging was extremely helpful in identifying distant disease, intra-operative planning, and further management.

papers.abstract: CT-based staging of the clinically node-negative (cN0) neck in oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC) has limited sensitivity, and occult nodal metastasis remains common. Whether the CT-to-surgery interval influences pathological nodal outcome is unclear. This retrospective study included 329 patients with primary cN0 OSCC undergoing CT staging and neck dissection (2011-2024). Associations with lymph node positivity, lymph node count, and extranodal extension (ENE) were assessed using logistic and negative binomial regression, with sensitivity analyses (quartiles, exclusion of extreme intervals, lymph node yield adjustment). Median CT-to-surgery interval was 9.0 days (IQR 5.0-15.0), and 53 patients (16.1%) had lymph node metastasis. The interval was associated with lymph node positivity in univariable analysis (OR 1.031, p = 0.035), but not after adjustment for age and smoking (OR 1.027, p = 0.065); lymph node count showed a similar non-significant association (IRR 1.027, p = 0.068). The association with nodal positivity was not robust across interval quartiles (p = 0.969), after excluding intervals >30 days (OR 0.995, p = 0.824), or after adjustment for lymph node yield (OR 1.015, p = 0.334). However, patients with intervals >30 days (n = 13) had higher nodal positivity than those with shorter intervals (53.8% vs. 14.6%). The interval was not associated with ENE (p = 0.740), and tumor localization was not associated with nodal positivity (p = 0.175). An initially significant, unadjusted association was not robust to sensitivity testing and was confined to a small subgroup with substantially prolonged intervals. This offers some reassurance that the CT-to-surgery interval is not strongly associated with occult nodal metastasis in cN0 OSCC, while substantially delayed surgery warrants further investigation.

papers.abstract: Following the EV-302/KEYNOTE-A39 study, the combination therapy of enfortumab vedotin and pembrolizumab (EV-P) has been established as a new first-line treatment for metastatic urothelial carcinoma. With increasing use, the documentation and publication of unexpected side effects and complications are essential to systematize procedures. We report on a 56-year-old patient who experienced an extravasation of EV-P during the first cycle due to dislocation of the port catheter from the cephalic vein. Extensive subcutaneous necrosis of the infraclavicular region required surgical debridement and application of a vacuum-assisted closure system, followed by secondary wound healing. The wound healed with a residual scar but no functional impairment or persistent pain. The therapy was resumed via a peripheral venous catheter, and the patient achieved a deep partial response. To our knowledge, this represents the first reported case of central venous EV-P extravasation (CTCAE grade 3) requiring surgical therapy. Because of its cytotoxic payload, EV in particular may pose a high risk of local complications in the context of extravasations.

papers.abstract: TAPUR is a phase II basket trial evaluating the antitumor activity of commercially available targeted agents in patients with advanced cancer and genomic alterations. Results of two cohorts of patients with advanced thyroid (TC) or biliary tract cancer (BTC) with BRAF V600E mutations treated with cobimetinib plus vemurafenib (C + V) are reported. Eligible patients had measurable disease (RECIST v1.1), Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group performance status 0-2, adequate organ function, and no standard treatment options. The primary end point was disease control (DC), defined as objective response (OR) or stable disease (SD) of at least 16+ weeks duration. Simon's two-stage design was based on a null DC rate of 15% versus 35% (power = 0.85; α = .10). Both cohorts expanded to stage II but closed before reaching the target sample size by pharmaceutical company request; inferences are based on thresholds set forth in the protocol to maintain the α level. Secondary end points included OR, progression-free survival, overall survival, duration of response, duration of SD, and safety. Patients with TC (N = 22; n = 16 evaluable) or BTC (N = 18; n = 15 evaluable) with BRAF V600E mutations were enrolled. In the TC cohort, the DC and OR rates were 94% (one-sided 90% CI, 78 to 100) and 63% (95% CI, 35 to 85), respectively. In the BTC cohort, the DC and OR rates were 67% (one-sided 90% CI, 47 to 100) and 53% (95% CI, 27 to 79), respectively. The null hypothesis of 15% DC rate was rejected for both cohorts (P < .0001). Twenty-one patients (53%) had ≥1 treatment-related grade 3 to 4 adverse event (AE) or serious AE. The combination of C + V met the prespecified criteria to declare a signal of activity in patients with TC and BTC with BRAF V600E mutations.

papers.abstract: BRCA1/2 mutation testing identifies patients with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer (mCRPC) eligible for poly(ADP-ribose) polymerase inhibitors; however, clinical outcomes remain heterogeneous within these genotypes. We evaluated whether plasma-derived genomic instability status (GIS) was associated with outcomes beyond BRCA1/2 and PALB2 mutation status in the phase II TRITON2 study. This retrospective biomarker analysis included TRITON2 patients with available baseline plasma profiled using Guardant360 Liquid. GIS is a probabilistic measure of homologous recombination deficiency (HRD) inferred from genome-wide copy number variants and somatic mutational signatures. Analyses were restricted to patients with baseline tumor fraction (TF) ≥ 25%. Radiographic progression-free survival (rPFS) was analyzed using Kaplan-Meier methods and Cox models adjusted for age and baseline TF. Secondary end points included objective response rate (ORR), serum prostate-specific antigen (PSA50) declines, and overall survival (OS). Among 104 patients with TF ≥ 25%, 43 (41%) had GIS detected. Compared with GIS detected, absence of GIS was associated with shorter rPFS (hazard ratio [HR], 2.81 [95% CI, 1.61 to 4.93]; P <.001). Joint stratification demonstrated patients with both GIS detected and BRCA/PALB2 mutation experienced the longest rPFS, whereas absence of GIS was associated with shorter rPFS regardless of BRCA/PALB2 mutation status. In BRCA2-mutated patients, rPFS trended being longer in those with GIS detected (compared with those without GIS detected; HR, 2.02 [95% CI, 0.95 to 4.29]; P = .069), with numerically higher ORR (25.7% v 14.3%) and PSA50 response rate (65.7% v 42.9%). No statistically significant differences in OS were observed. Plasma-derived GIS was associated with improved rPFS and higher response rates in rucaparib-treated patients and further stratified outcomes within mutation-defined populations. These findings support genomic instability assessment as a complementary biomarker to mutation testing and warrant prospective validation.

papers.abstract: Forcing together with radiative responses and natural variability has sharply increased Earth's energy imbalance (EEI), a key driver of climate change, between 2003 and 2023. Declining anthropogenic aerosol emissions and increasing greenhouse gas concentrations are the leading contributors to the forcing. However, observation-based and model-based forcing estimates disagree on the magnitude of aerosol forcing, particularly for effective radiative forcing from aerosol-cloud interactions (ERFACI). Here, we show that two independent observation-based estimates of forcing trends achieve unexpectedly good closure between 2003 and 2023. The corresponding model-based trend is within the uncertainty range of observations but substantially smaller, with most of the difference due to models' underestimation of cloud fraction adjustment to aerosols. Our results suggest a prominent role of aerosols in the recent EEI increase and stronger total historical ERFACI and higher equilibrium climate sensitivity than the current consensus, with a likely range between 2.8° and 4.8°C.
